notes: Unary and binary minus have separate operator helper identities; real Dart wrappers preserve native dispatch, equality/null and argument checking.

Pre-created super bridges dispatch unary/binary/index operators to their actual ancestor. A typed generated index forwarding object preserves index evaluation once, get/RHS/set order, assignment results, short circuit, prefix/postfix and await RHS behavior.
Operator changes retain original classes and AOT main/invoke/negative/dynamicOps/equal/churn. New Added operator executes through old AOT consumers and survives GC.
IndexChild.addedSuper first uses super index multiplication in patch code without changing its class. Generic Strings.append also executes super-index code from patch bytecode.

Removing an index setter relocates Base/Child and retires only the unused generated adapter after a current-reference check; the old adapter class remains in the baseline snapshot. User class deletion remains rejected.
An exploratory non-void []= declaration was correctly rejected by original-source analysis. The final fixture uses void and a regression requires non-void rejection.
This increment rebuilt normal, GC, operators, operator-removal, dynamic index checks and mixins. It did not rebuild every historical native fixture.

An initial property adapter incorrectly evaluated the RHS before rejecting a bad dynamic index. That native counterexample is preserved in output/m1-operator-checks-initial.log. The old ordinary verification was cancelled and is not acceptance evidence; final source uses exact index parameter types and native []/[]= syntax.
The index adapter introduces temporary closures/objects; performance has not been measured.
